newsitem.title: USA: CBOT CORN ENDS UP ON OUTLOOKS FOR DRIER WEATHER.
newsitem.headline: CBOT CORN ENDS UP ON OUTLOOKS FOR DRIER WEATHER.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed higher on a rebound tied to signals the market was oversold and on rekindled concerns about dry weather in portions of the U.S. Midwest, traders said.

"The only thing in here today was the dry weather. Weather Services never has been wet, they were dry Monday and they're still dry which is what I'm banking on," said Tom Levis, analyst for Prudential Securities.
Corn futures dropped sharply early this week on some forecasts for rain by the weekend in key U.S. Midwest corn growing states.
But Weather Services Corp senior agricultural meteorologist David Taylor early Wednesday said the showers may be lightest in the areas where corn and soybean crops most need moisture.

"Right now it looks like we will have the hardest time getting decent rain in the Illinois and Indiana area," he said, noting rainfall of 0.25 to 1.00 inch was expected over the weekend in the Midwest with 40 to 60 percent coverage.
Corn closed 1/2 to 4-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with September up 4-1/2 at $2.59 a bushel. New crop December closed 4-1/4 cents higher at $2.61-1/2.

The market also was undergoing position squaring amid forecasts for the 1997 U.S. corn crop. Trade sources Tuesday said Sparks Companies estimated 1997 U.S. corn production at 9.47 billion bushels, below USDA's forecast in July for 9.7 billion.
Corn production forecasts also are expected to be released this week by Farmers Commodities Corp and the Leslie-ADM Elevator Survey.
At 0730 CDT Tuesday, the U.S. Agriculture Department will release its August crop production and supply/demand reports.
In spread dealings, Cargill Inc did 1.2 million bushels of September/December at three cents, premium Dec, traders said.
Refco Inc bought six million bushesl of December, Prudential Securities bought six million December and Cargill Investor Services sold six million December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 72,000 contracts, below the 79,225 traded Tuesday.

In corn options, Prudential Securities bought 700 September $2.40 puts at one to 1-1/8 cents, Farmers Commodities sold 850 September $2.40 puts at one to 1-1/8 cents and bought 1,000 September $2.30 puts at 5/8 cent, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, below the 22,073 traded Tuesday.
